Subject: Audit request: access/audit log retention and extract options

Hi Ava —

We’re kicking off our annual compliance collection for EchoTech and need a few clarifications around Redwood’s audit/access logs:

1) Retention windows for both access logs and admin/audit logs (what’s kept by default in hosted vs. dedicated vs. private deployments?).
2) Export formats you support for handover (NDJSON/CSV/Parquet?), and whether exports include full request/response metadata and IP/residency fields.
3) Residency guarantees for exported data (we need an EU-only export path for our EU tenant).
4) Deletion attestation: we may need a signed statement that specific tenant logs were deleted after an export for legal retention lifecycles — do you provide an erase certification?

We’d appreciate a quick run-down and a sample export spec (schema) so our audit team can validate ingestion. Target: evidence package by Oct 16.

Subject: Re: Audit request: access/audit log retention and extract options

Hi Jon —

Thanks — happy to help. Short answers up front, followed by a proposed delivery plan (we’ll attach a sample NDJSON extract schema).

Short answers:
- Retention: Hosted API (default): 30 days for request/response traces and 365 days for anonymized usage aggregates. Dedicated/Private deployments: configurable; customers commonly keep 90–730 days depending on the contract and region.
- Export formats: NDJSON (recommended for event streams), CSV (field-limited), Parquet (columnar, bulk analytics). Exports include timestamp, model_id, route_id, request_id, user_agent, src_ip (where allowed by residency/privacy config), and full request/response metadata unless the tenant has redaction enabled.
- Residency: For EU tenants we support an EU-only export path — data is streamed to an EU S3 bucket under your control (or our managed EU export bucket with encryption + tenant isolation).
- Deletion attestation: We can provide an erase attestation template (signed by Redwood operations) after we run the deletion workflow for the tenant’s retained artifacts. For Private deployments, attestation can be executed by the tenant’s admin if running on-prem.

Proposed delivery plan
1) Today: confirm the exact tenant ID and the time window you need exported (e.g., 2025-10-01 → 2026-09-30).
2) By Tue (Oct 12): we’ll deliver a sample NDJSON export (schema + 48-hour test extract) for your ingestion tests — attached: redwood_log_export_spec_v1.ndjson.
3) By Fri (Oct 16): full evidence package (export files in EU S3, MD5 checksums, and erase attestation script run notes).

Notes/limits: exports that contain src_ip will be gated by your tenant residency flags and applicable data protection laws; for some EU countries we offer IP truncation to the /24 where requested. Also, for very large exports we advise a staged run (daily slices) to avoid prolonged impact on inference nodes.

I’ve looped in Marissa (legal / contracts point) and Grace (ops / export owner) to scope work and confirm timelines.

— Ava
Ava Chen
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
